summary: Edge replay + prewarm drift latches tenant to degraded model variant during canary
description:
Issue summary: NovusHealth reports that during a staged canary for redwood-v2-small the tenant's traffic was redirected to a degraded quantized variant and stayed pinned there even after canary rollback. Impact: customer experienced ~30% increase in latency tails and a small increase in hallucination-style tokenization artifacts. This is customer-facing latency/quality regression affecting a handful of active production tenants.

Environment: production (dedicated pool) in us-east-1. Canary was a traffic-slice weighted rollout (10% -> 30%) with prewarm enabled.

Steps to reproduce (customer-reported):
1) Trigger a weighted canary promoting redwood-v2-small to slot X with prewarm mirror enabled.
2) Initiate an edge replay for a set of long-lived streaming sessions (customer uses keepalive / reconnect pattern).
3) Observe that subsequent requests from the same tenant are routed to the quantized fallback variant (redwood-v2-quantized) rather than the pinned promotion even after rollback.

Observed behavior: Tenant traffic remains routed to degraded/quantized variant and does not rebind to the original pinned version for ~12-18 minutes. Metrics show prewarm mirror state indicating a partial commit but orchestrator snapshot shows no full commit. Edge-proxy logs contain replay markers and a header X-Edge-Replay: 1.

Expected behavior: Edge replays should be treated as idempotent probes that do not change pin state. Rollbacks should restore prior pinned routing within the configured pin_grace_period (<1m).

Logs/telemetry provided:
- Excerpted edge headers: "X-Edge-Replay: 1", "X-Session-KV: tenant-12345", "X-Prewarm-State: partial-commit"
- Orchestrator snapshot ids: snapshot-20260310-17:24:07 (prewarm partial), snapshot-20260310-17:25:12 (rollback)
- Dashboard links: https://dash.redwood.ai/tenants/novushealth/requests?from=2026-03-10T17:20Z&to=2026-03-10T17:40Z
comments: 2026-03-10 18:02 - NovusHealth (support contact): 'We see our streaming sessions redirected to a slower quantized model after a canary rollback. Sessions keep reconnecting; traffic is stuck for ~15 minutes. Please advise.'

2026-03-10 18:25 - Support (Aisha Gupta): 'Thanks for the report. We're triaging. Can you confirm whether the client is resending the original session cookie on reconnect? Also sending your tenant id to engineering.'

2026-03-11 09:12 - Eng (Marco Hernandez): 'Reproduced in staging with a mirrored prewarm + simulated edge replay. Edge replay increments replay-counter and triggers an incomplete prewarm merge path in orchestrator which leaves a tombstone in the snapshot index. That tombstone causes routing to prefer the quantized variant until epoch reconciliation runs.'

2026-03-11 14:41 - Support (Aisha Gupta): 'Customer confirmed they use keepalive with reconnects and do not reissue a new session cookie. They are on a dedicated pool and expect no routing changes after rollback.'

2026-03-12 08:03 - Eng (Marco Hernandez): 'Implemented a temporary guard: ignore replay-marked requests when computing prewarm commit decisions. Rolling a hotfix to edge-proxy and orchestrator in staging now.'

2026-03-13 02:16 - Support (Aisha Gupta): 'Applied customer-side mitigation: instruct client to send a forced session-refresh header after rollback to re-establish pinning; customer reports immediate restoration for affected sessions.'
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge replay requests with X-Edge-Replay cause the prewarm mirror to create partial commit entries which get interpreted as a valid fallback by the routing mesh.
Hypothesis 2: Tombstones left by partial prewarm merges are not garbage-collected until shard-epoch reconciliation, producing a transient preference for quantized variants.
Commands/runbooks used: curl to replay endpoint, kubectl logs -n edge edge-proxy-*, redis-cli HGETALL prewarm:tenant-12345, gcloud monitoring queries for tail-latency spikes.

Key observation: orchestrator commit path expects a "commit_ack" from serving nodes. Edge replay paths currently skip commit_ack acking which leaves commit in 'pending' state but with a routing fallback entry present.

Telemetry: spike in 'routing.fallback.rate' from 0.02% to 1.8% during replay window. 'pin.rebind.latency' shows median 90s, p99 14m for affected tenant.
Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/trace?query=snapshot-20260310
Related code areas: prewarm merger (orchestrator/service/prewarm_merge.go), edge-replay handling (edge-proxy/handlers/replay.go), snapshot tombstone GC (orchestrator/persistence/gc.go).
Reproducible in staging with synthetic keepalive pattern and replaying same session id with 'X-Edge-Replay: 1' header. Verified fix reduces pin rebind time to <30s in staging tests.
resolution_notes: Workaround (customer-facing): Instruct client to issue a session-refresh (POST /session/refresh) immediately after rollback to force a new pin handshake. This was communicated and validated by NovusHealth; it restored routing within seconds.

Short-term fix deployed to staging: ignore X-Edge-Replay when computing prewarm commit eligibility and require explicit commit_ack from serving nodes before writing routing fallback entries. Patch applied to edge-proxy v0.9.8-canary and orchestrator v1.4.2-hotfix.

Planned production rollout: hotfix to be applied to us-east-1 dedicated pools during a low-traffic window 2026-03-15 02:00-03:00 UTC with canary traffic at 1% for 30m, monitor 'pin.rebind.latency' and 'routing.fallback.rate'.

Postmortem actions: (1) Add unit/integration test for replay path and prewarm commits; (2) Add GC sweep for partial prewarm tombstones to accelerate cleanup; (3) Update canary runbook to include explicit replay-header handling; (4) Docs update for dedicated customers describing expected client behavior for keepalive/reconnect patterns.
Follow-ups created: INT-4132 (eng task to add tests), SUP-2060820 (customer follow-up to confirm post-rollout behavior).
Status: hotfix validated in staging, customer workaround confirmed. Production rollout scheduled; ticket will be updated after canary completes.
